name: AI Chat - Local LLM
description: Sends a prompt from each record to a language model on your own server, through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and adds the reply as a Response field.
introductoryText:
![LLM](data:image/png;base64,)

Sends the prompt in each record to a language model served on your own machine or network through an **OpenAI-compatible** chat completions endpoint (as offered by llama.cpp, llamafile, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM and others) and adds the reply to the record, in a **Response** field, with a **Truncated** field that is true when a reply was cut short.

**To set it up**

1. Enter the **Endpoint**: the server's address ending in `/v1`, for example `http://localhost:8080/v1`. The address is resolved on the Omniscope server, not your browser; if Omniscope runs Python in Docker, `localhost` is the container.
2. Enter the **Model** name your server expects (servers that hold one model ignore it).
3. Choose the **User prompt field**, and optionally a **System prompt field** with the instructions.

Prompts are sent several at a time (Requests at a time, under Advanced). If any request fails, the block stops with the service's error message and no output.

The data goes only to the endpoint you enter. Requests at a time is 1 by default, as many local servers answer one request at a time.

options.name: ModelEndpoint
options.title: Endpoint
options.description: The base address of an OpenAI-compatible API, usually ending in /v1, for example http://localhost:8080/v1 (llama.cpp, llamafile) or http://localhost:11434/v1 (Ollama). Resolved on the Omniscope server.

options.name: ApiKey
options.title: API key
options.description: Optional. Only if your server asks for one; most local servers don't.

options.name: Model
options.title: Model
options.description: The model name your server expects, for example the name listed by its /v1/models page. Servers that hold one model (llama.cpp, llamafile) accept any name.

options.name: Prompt
options.title: User prompt field
options.description: The field holding each record's prompt: the instruction and the text to work on. Build it with a Formula block if it combines several fields. Numbers and dates are sent as text; records with an empty prompt are not sent.

options.name: SystemPrompt
options.title: System prompt field
options.description: Optional. A field holding instructions that set the model's role, rules and answer format, for example "Reply with one category only: Billing, Delivery or Other". Usually the same text on every record.

options.name: Temperature
options.title: Temperature
options.description: Optional, 0 to 2. Lower values make replies more consistent, higher values more varied. Leave empty to use the model's default. Some servers cap it at 1 or ignore it.

options.name: MaxTokens
options.title: Maximum response length (tokens)
options.description: Optional. The most tokens each reply may use. A token is roughly three-quarters of a word. Replies that reach the limit are cut short and marked in the Truncated field. Empty: the server's default.

options.name: Concurrency
options.title: Requests at a time
options.description: How many requests are sent at the same time, 1 to 16. Higher finishes large inputs sooner; lower it if the service reports a rate limit. Most local servers answer one request at a time unless set up for more.

blockOutputs.label: Replies
blockOutputs.tooltip: The input records with two fields added: Response (the model's reply) and Truncated (true if the reply stopped at the maximum response length). Records with an empty prompt have both empty.
